newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Unisource partners in international telecom merger.
newsitem.headline: Unisource partners in international telecom merger.

text.p: European telecoms joint venture Unisource NV said on Wednesday its three partners were binding themselves closer together by merging their international networks to create a $2.0 billion-a-year business.

Unisource -- which groups PTT Telecom of the Netherlands, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT -- said the move would lead to cost-savings of up to 30 percent which would be passed on to customers in lower tariffs.

"We are creating a multi-billion (dollar) company which further expands our presence in Europe and puts us in a leading position in the global telecommunications wholesale market," Unisource president Paul Smits said.

The three partners will merge their separate international networks into Unisource Carrier Services (UCS) as of January 1, 1998. UCS will have 900 employees, up from around 200 at present, and will have its headquarters in Switzerland.
"By doing this there will be rationalisation benefits, the cost level will go down 20-30 percent," Smits said.
Smits said Unisource could attract more business as it integrated the three networks, eliminating duplication, slashing overheads and enabling it to offer lower tariffs to customers.

"The overriding thing is that in the new arena it's everything to do with being competitive, having large volumes, extremely slim organisations, dealing with the newest technology, offering extremely low tariffs," he said.
Unisource noted that completion of the merger would coincide with the European Union's date for liberalisation of European telecommunications services.
"By further strengthening our carrier business we are ideally positioned to take maximum advantage of the opportunities the liberalised...market will present," it said.
Unisource said the UCS network could eventually be linked to that of AT&T Corp, with whom it operates a business telecoms joint venture, to create a truly global network.
Smits said Unisource might add a fourth European partner at some future date but was not desperate to replace the Spanish firm Telefonica.
Telefonica was asked to leave Unisource after joining the rival Concert alliance which groups British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp.
"We are not desperately seeking a fourth partner. It's a pity the Telefonica thing happened but that's that," said Smits.
